text: Container Insights is Azure Monitor's view into a cluster — most commonly AKS. Enabling it deploys the Azure Monitor agent as a containerized DaemonSet on every node, the modern replacement for the older omsagent, shipping performance data, inventory, and logs to the same Log Analytics workspace from Lesson 1. Everything it collects is queryable with the exact KQL you already learned.

The agent collects at every layer that matters for a Kubernetes workload, by default on a one-minute interval: node-level CPU, memory, and disk; pod-level status and resource usage; and container-level CPU and memory, down to one specific container inside a pod. That three-layer view is what lets you tell whether a problem is the node, the pod, or one container within it.

KubePodInventory records every pod's phase, namespace, and scheduled node, which makes a query like this a real rollout health check: filter to Failed or Pending pods, group by namespace and status, bucket it hourly. That's exactly the kind of query you'd run while chasing a deployment that isn't converging, and it uses the same summarize and bin pattern from Lesson 2.

For container-level detail, Perf carries counters like cpuUsageNanoCores, scoped by InstanceName instead of a VM's Computer field — the same summarize, bin, and render timechart pattern, now isolating one container's CPU usage over time. ContainerLogV2 carries each container's raw stdout and stderr, the current, more efficient schema replacing the older ContainerLog table.

Live Data streams pod logs, Kubernetes events, and exec access directly in the portal in close to real time — the AKS equivalent of Application Insights' Live Metrics, useful for watching a pod the moment it starts crash-looping without a local kubectl session already configured.

One closing point: Container Insights is also a real cost driver, because ContainerLogV2 and high-cardinality Perf data can generate a large volume of billed ingestion if every container's verbose output is collected at full fidelity everywhere. Data collection rules scope exactly what gets collected by namespace or log level — a decision this chapter hands off directly to the FinOps material later in the course. Next chapter does all of this again, on the AWS side, with CloudWatch.
